# 2 Chronicles Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Solomon son of David secured his grip on the kingdom. The LORD his God was with him and made him extraordinarily powerful.

**2** Solomon summoned all Israel — the commanders of thousands and hundreds, the judges, every leader, and all the heads of families.

**3** Solomon and the whole assembly went to the worship center at Gibeon, because that was where God's tent of meeting stood — the one Moses the LORD's servant had made in the wilderness.

**4** (David had already moved the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim to the tent he had set up for it in Jerusalem.

**5** But the bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made was still at Gibeon in front of the LORD's tabernacle.) Solomon and the assembly went there to seek God.

**6** Solomon went up to the bronze altar before the LORD at the tent of meeting and sacrificed a thousand burnt offerings on it.

**7** That night God appeared to Solomon and said, "Ask for whatever you want me to give you."

**8** Solomon replied, "You showed enormous faithfulness to my father David, and now You have made me king in his place.

**9** LORD God, fulfill the promise You made to my father David, for You have made me king over a people as numerous as dust.

**10** Give me wisdom and knowledge to lead this people, because who could possibly govern this great nation of Yours?"

**11** God said to Solomon, "Because your deepest desire was for this — you didn't ask for wealth, riches, fame, the death of your enemies, or even a long life, but instead asked for wisdom and knowledge to govern My people over whom I've made you king —

**12** wisdom and knowledge are yours. And I will also give you wealth, riches, and fame beyond anything the kings before you had, and beyond anything those after you will have."

**13** Solomon returned to Jerusalem from the worship center at Gibeon, from the tent of meeting, and ruled over Israel.

**14** Solomon built up his military forces: fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen. He stationed them in the chariot cities and with him in Jerusalem.

**15** The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stone, and cedar as abundant as sycamore-fig trees in the foothills.

**16** Solomon's horses were imported from Egypt and from Kue — the royal merchants purchased them from Kue at the going rate.

**17** A chariot could be imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty. They also exported them to all the Hittite and Aramean kings.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **1:7**: God's blank-check offer — "Ask for whatever you want" — is one of the most dramatic moments in Scripture. Solomon's response reveals his character: he asks for the tools to serve, not the rewards of power.

- **1:10**: Solomon asks for wisdom to "go out and come in" — Hebrew idiom for leadership, especially military leadership. He's not asking to be clever; he's asking to be competent for an impossible job.

- **1:15**: Silver as common as rocks, cedar as common as scrub trees — the narrator wants you to understand that Solomon's wealth was beyond anything the ancient world had seen.


— PNEUMA
